summary: Mission Control 3D: NASA Missions is an interactive, browser-based 3D educational spaceflight simulation built with Three.js and WebAudio that lets players command 15 historic NASA missions—from Mercury Friendship 7 and Apollo 11 to Voyager 2, James Webb Space Telescope, DART, and Artemis I.   Each mission unfolds across three distinct phases: Launch, Deep-Space Cruise, and Arrival. Powered by simplified real-world physics models—including exponential atmospheric density, aerodynamic drag and lift, Sutton–Graves convective heat flux calculations, and gravity-assist trajectories—players experience authentic aerospace challenges such as managing structural loads during Max Q, executing atmospheric skip-entry guidance, performing unpowered Space Shuttle landings, and making real-time Flight Director GO/NO-GO telemetry decisions.   By turning complex orbital mechanics and spaceflight engineering into an accessible, hands-on game requiring zero installation, the project inspires students and space enthusiasts to explore the science behind NASA's greatest achievements.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Mission Control 3D: NASA Missions is an interactive, browser-based 3D educational spaceflight simulation where players command 15 historic NASA missions spanning from 1962 to 2024—including Mercury Friendship 7, Apollo 11, Viking 1, Voyager 2, STS-1 Columbia, Hubble, STS-71 Atlantis–Mir, Mars Pathfinder, Cassini–Huygens, New Horizons, Parker Solar Probe, Mars 2020 Perseverance, DART, James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), and Artemis I.

Each mission is structured into three continuous flight phases:

  1. Launch & Ascent: Players steer along the ascent corridor, manage structural loads ($q \cdot \alpha < 200\text{ kPa}\cdot^\circ$) through wind shear and Max Q (maximum dynamic pressure), and manually trigger stage separations and payload fairing jettisons.
  2. Deep-Space Cruise: Players navigate 3D orbital trajectories, hit golden gravity-assist gates around planets such as Venus, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus to gain velocity, and unlock real-time historical mission logs.
  3. Arrival & Specialized Finales: Depending on the mission, players execute one of seven distinct engineering challenges—powered planetary landings, Sky Crane rover deployment, ballistic retrofire and Orion skip-entry guidance using live altitude/range predictors, unpowered Space Shuttle runway gliding, centimeter-precision RCS docking with Mir, solar umbra keeping inside the Sun's corona, flyby imaging with motion compensation, kinetic asteroid impact, or Flight Director GO / NO-GO telemetry reviews.

Benefits & Intended Impact Complex aerospace concepts such as atmospheric density gradients, convective heat flux, gravity assists, and orbital $\Delta V$ budgets often remain abstract in traditional classrooms. By turning real NASA mission profiles and post-flight performance comparisons into a hands-on, zero-installation experience, the project makes spaceflight engineering intuitive, engaging, and accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

Tools, Technologies & Coding Languages

  • Languages & Web Standards: HTML5, CSS3, and modern JavaScript (ES6+).
  • 3D Graphics & Shaders: Three.js (WebGL) with ACES Filmic tone mapping, real-time shadow maps, and custom GLSL atmospheric scattering shaders.
  • Procedural Audio & Textures: WebAudio API for synthesized engine rumble, wind buffeting, RCS thruster puffs, and Quindar tones; 3D Fractional Brownian Motion (fBM) noise on HTML5 Canvas for planetary surfaces, cloud layers, and terrain.
  • Hosting: Deployed as a self-contained static web application on GitHub Pages ([https://murat-tr.github.io/gorev-kontrol-3d/](https://murat-tr.github.io/gorev-kontrol-3d/)).

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Simplified Real-World Physics: Incorporates an exponential atmosphere model ($\rho = \rho_0 e^{-h/H}$), aerodynamic drag and lift equations, and the Sutton–Graves convective heat flux equation ($\dot{q} = k\sqrt{\rho/R_n}V^3$), balanced with scaled game timelines so missions remain scientifically authentic yet playable in minutes.
  • Zero-Dependency Portability & Accessibility: All 11 rockets, 13 spacecraft, textures, and sound effects are generated procedurally in code—eliminating external asset loading delays and supporting both desktop keyboard controls (WASD/Arrows, Space, G/N, C, Shift) and mobile multi-touch virtual joysticks.
  • Historical Authenticity: Incorporates real mission anomalies—such as Hubble's stuck solar array and JWST's tensioner motor temperature spike—teaching players how NASA flight controllers diagnose telemetry under pressure.
